summary: The current failures cluster around fractional-second conversion in `absl/time/format.cc`: formatting multiplies the subsecond representation before passing femtoseconds to CCTZ, and parsing converts CCTZ femtoseconds back before constructing an Abseil duration. The observed formatted fractions are exactly four times the expected values, but the supplied excerpts do not establish the representation units or rounding and boundary behavior needed to identify a safe repair.
hypotheses: `Split()` scales `GetRepLo()` by the wrong factor when converting Abseil duration units to CCTZ femtoseconds, causing the fourfold formatting error.
`Join()` converts parsed femtoseconds to the wrong `MakeDuration()` low-part units, causing fractional parse results to diverge.
A shared duration representation or accessor change altered the contract of `GetRepLo()` or `MakeDuration()`, affecting both conversion directions.
